title: She lost her sight before her board exams. She just argued a case in India's Supreme Court. September 30, 2026.
excerpt: From a submarine India built without knowing how, to a chip India grew from a wafer up, September 30's five stories share one thread: every one of them started by doing something nobody around them had done before.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about a genuine first - not a marketing claim, a real one. A submarine built with no domestic precedent, a healthcare executive handed an entirely new job title, an astronaut with two immigrant parents from opposite sides of the world, a chip fabricated from raw material up, and a blind law graduate arguing in a courtroom no blind woman had argued in before.

September 30, 1989: India launched a submarine it had never built before - and built it anyway

INS Shalki was launched on September 30, 1989, at Mazagon Dock Limited, Bombay - India's first indigenously built submarine, a Shishumar-class vessel built under a technology transfer agreement with Germany's HDW. Raw materials like HY-80 steel came from abroad, but all cutting, forming and welding was done domestically. It was commissioned into Indian Navy service on February 7, 1992.

He led a database company for less than a year. Then Mark Zuckerberg created a role for him at Meta

Chirantan 'CJ' Desai stepped down as President and CEO of MongoDB on September 28, 2026, to become Meta's Chief Enterprise Platform Officer - a newly created role heading a division that turns Meta's AI capabilities into products for developers and businesses, reporting directly to Mark Zuckerberg. Before MongoDB, Desai spent nearly 8 years at ServiceNow, growing its revenue from $1.5 billion to over $10 billion.

His father is from Kerala. His mother is from Ukraine. In July 2026, he launched to the International Space Station

NASA astronaut Anil Menon launched on his first spaceflight aboard Soyuz MS-29 on July 14, 2026, from Baikonur Cosmodrome, for an approximately 8-month mission. Before becoming an astronaut, he spent years as a NASA flight surgeon and was SpaceX's first flight surgeon and medical director. He was born in Minneapolis to a father who immigrated from Ottapalam, Kerala, and a mother who immigrated from Ukraine.

India just built a chip that runs 300 times faster than the silicon in most electronics

DRDO's Solid State Physics Laboratory has indigenously developed Gallium Nitride semiconductor chips for next-generation radar and electronic warfare systems - a 3.5x3mm chip delivering up to 30 watts, built on indigenously grown 4-inch Silicon Carbide wafers, with some components reaching 150 watts. Limited production capability has already been set up at GAETEC, Hyderabad, targeting defense, aerospace and 5G applications.

She lost her sight completely right before her board exams. She just became the first blind woman to argue a case before India's Supreme Court

Anchal Bhateja was born with low vision that worsened until she lost her eyesight entirely just before her Class X exams. She completed schooling using audiobooks, topped Class XII, and became the first visually impaired student admitted to the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru. On June 6, 2025, she became the first blind woman to argue a case before the Supreme Court of India, challenging a recruitment rule that excluded blindness from disability-reserved judicial seats.

Five stories, one thread: a submarine built with no domestic template to follow, an executive role invented specifically for one person, an astronaut carrying two immigrant stories into orbit, a chip grown from raw wafer material rather than assembled, and a courtroom argument no blind woman had made before. Every one of them is a genuine first - the kind that only counts once someone actually does it.
